correctness.rationale: For the Cartesian prism of two n-cliques, a zero in each layer makes the zero set dominating. Every maximal function therefore has both layers positive, or exactly one zero-containing layer with some positive vertex. Positive-layer conditions reduce to a single high-label test. Partition the other layer into at least one 3 or two 2s, exactly one 2 and no 3, or zero 2s/3s; the four exact polynomial factors count disjoint configurations and witness requirements. Minimum degree comparison yields n+4 and exactly 2n^2 optima for n>=4. Two explicit subfamilies cover all integer weights n+4 through 6n. Direct 4^(2n) enumeration through n=6 agrees coefficientwise with independently convolved symbolic formula; symbolic total/interval checks reach n=14. The proof, not the finite checks, establishes all-n statements.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2022 maximal double Roman article was inspected through its open full preprint and gives general bounds, algorithmic results, trees, paths and cycles, not the complete weight enumerator on two-clique prisms. The 2023 survey section on maximal double Roman domination likewise gives general results but no such polynomial. Nearby concrete findings distinguish cocktail-party graphs (same invariant, different graph) from complete-prism quasi-total double Roman domination (same graph, different admissibility). A broad-coverage algorithm that could compute a finite instance does not itself give the displayed closed formula for all n. Historical priority remains provisional, especially outside indexed research records.
residual_risks: Older exact results may exist in unindexed papers or tables.

value.rationale: A closed full weight polynomial on an infinite natural matching-linked two-clique graph family is a stronger enumerative result than a scalar optimum. The optimizer geometry is fully rigid and has exactly 2n^2 labelled realizations; the feasible-weight spectrum has no gaps. The three one-sided defender regimes and non-domination witness correction explain what changes when the two complete layers are matched. Exact coefficients and total counts provide a reproducible reference for the named invariant, independent of claims about applications.
